subject: Request: temporary p95 adjustment and measurement evidence for hosted API
body_text:
From: Ethan Blake <ethan.blake@finoptics.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: p95 boundary and measurement clarification for pilot

Vanessa —

Thanks for the demo last week. We ran a few extended load tests against the hosted endpoint and are seeing consistent p50 numbers in line with your benchmarks but p95 spikes that are higher than anticipated during short bursts (2–4 minute windows). Our SREs asked whether Redwood can provide a temporary carveout or relaxed p95 window for the initial 60-day pilot while we iterate on prompt-level caching and routing.

Can you outline what evidence you’d need to evaluate a partial exception (e.g., traces, histogram buckets, request-level metadata), and what an acceptable mitigation plan from our side would look like? We also want to avoid permanent SLA changes — this would be strictly limited to the pilot.

Best,
Ethan
SRE Manager, FinOptics

---

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Blake <ethan.blake@finoptics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: p95 boundary and measurement clarification for pilot

Ethan —

Appreciate the clear summary and congrats on getting the pilot rolling. Short answers up front: yes, we can evaluate a time-limited p95 accommodation for the pilot; yes, we will need a specific evidence packet; and yes, we prefer an engineering mitigation plan and measurable gates rather than a blanket SLA change.

High-level ask from our side so we can process this internally:
- Attach the request histogram (per-minute) covering the burst windows (you sent a sample PDF; the raw histogram CSV is ideal).
- Share 5 representative request traces (preferably with request_id and full header/context) for both a median and a p95 sample.
- Confirm the traffic pattern: are these bursts correlated to a specific route/model/sequence-length distribution?

Proposed operational approach (recommended):
1) Evidence intake: you provide the artifacts above within 5 business days.
2) Canary rule: we run a 14-day rolling evaluation window on our side to verify root cause and reproducibility.
3) Temporary SLO: if evidence shows bursty tails driven by client-side sequencing, we can offer a 30–60 day temporary p95 stretch in contract language limited to the pilot environment only. During that period we’ll require weekly telemetry check-ins and a mitigation milestone on your side (e.g., batching/prefix-cache rollout or routing rule).
4) Rollback and audit: Redwood will revert to standard p95 commitments after the temporary period unless both sides agree to a permanent amendment.

I’ve looped in Ben (technical) and Marissa (legal) to scope what we need and to prepare a succinct amendment draft. I’ll put together a short evidence checklist and a contract skeleton.

If that workflow looks reasonable, we can kickoff immediately.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

---

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Blake <ethan.blake@finoptics.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: p95 boundary and measurement clarification for pilot

Ethan —

Quick technical note from my side on what will help us debug and qualify a temporary p95 adjustment:
- Per-request metadata: model name + version, prompt token length, sequence length, request_id, region, and any custom routing tags.
- Traces: full span-level traces (start/end timestamps per stage: ingress, routing, kernel execution, kv-cache hit/miss).
- Histograms: 1-minute and 5-minute percentile buckets for the affected routes, and a short summary of concurrent QPS during the spike.
- Triage hint: include a sample of keys that were large (if applicable) — often long system prompts or attachments inflate processing time.

A couple of things we will test on our side while we evaluate your packet:
- Verify whether the tail events align with preemption/eviction on the hosting tier or with high-context-length kernel slowdowns.
- Run a controlled canary to replicate your traffic shape (we can do this with synthetic replay if you provide traces).

If you want, we can share an anonymized example of the telemetry artifacts we need (I’ll attach a template CSV after this thread).

— Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

---

From: legal@finoptics.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: p95 boundary and measurement clarification for pilot

Vanessa / Marissa —

FinOptics legal here. We’re willing to accept a pilot-limited SLA variation, but need clarity on: scope (which endpoints/routes), exact measurement windows, and an explicit termination date. Also request a clause that Redwood will provide weekly telemetry exports for the pilot period and that no permanent change to commercial SLAs occurs without a signed amendment.

Please propose specific wording for the amendment and the telemetry export schedule.

Regards,
L. Mendoza
Contracts Counsel, FinOptics

---

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Blake <ethan.blake@finoptics.com>, legal@finoptics.com, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 16:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: p95 boundary and measurement clarification for pilot

Team —

Thanks — aligned on scope and next steps. Action items I’m capturing here:
- FinOptics: upload the raw histograms (per-minute CSV) and 5 request traces by EOD 2026-12-07. Use the attached template (finoptics-evidence-request.xlsx) for consistency.
- Redwood (Ben): produce a telemetry template and synthetic-replay checklist by 2026-12-03 (Ben will attach template CSV).
- Redwood (Legal/Marissa): I’ve attached a 30-day pilot amendment draft (redwood-proposed-amendment-20261202.docx). Marissa, can you confirm the amendment includes:
    * Scope limited to specified routes/models and pilot key(s) only
    * Measurement method: rolling 14-day evaluation window for evidence intake, 1-minute percentile buckets for p50/p95, and explicit exclusion for outlier events caused by upstream third-party outages
    * Pilot duration: 30 days (option to extend to 60 days upon mutual written agreement)
    * Telemetry schedule: weekly exports (CSV) and a DocuSign-attested acceptance for the temporary change

If everyone is good with the checklist, we’ll accept the packet and trigger the canary evaluation. Marissa — if you could make two small edits (scope clarifications and a rollback sentence) and reattach for signature, we’ll route to FinOptics legal.

Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: finoptics-evidence-request.xlsx, redwood-proposed-amendment-20261202.docx, request-histogram-202611.pdf
